title.en: Volume 432 Biographies 219: Xiao Qijiang, Zhang Yunlan, Tang Xunfang, Jiang Ningxue, Chen Shi, Li Yuandu
title.raw: 卷432 列傳二百十九 萧启江 张运兰 唐训方 蒋凝学 陈湜 李元度

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十九

translations.literal: Biographies 219
translations.idiomatic: Biography 219

sentences.zh: 蕭啟江張運蘭唐訓方蔣凝學陳湜李元度

translations.literal: Xiao Qijiang, Zhang Yunlan, Tang Xunfang, Jiang Ningxue, Chen Shi, Li Yuandu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qijiang, Zhang Yunlan, Tang Xunfang, Jiang Ningxue, Chen Shi, and Li Yuandu

sentences.zh: 蕭啟江，字濬川，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xiao Qijiang, styled Junchuan, was a man of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qijiang, whose courtesy name was Junchuan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 少賈於蜀，後始折節讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he traded in Shu; only later did he restrain himself and take up study.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he went into trade in Sichuan; only later did he turn to serious study.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，入塔齊布軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he entered the army of Taqibu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he joined the forces under Taqibu.

sentences.zh: 四年，從平岳州，克武昌、漢陽、興國、大冶、蘄州，敘縣丞，晉秩州同。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed in the pacification of Yuezhou, captured Wuchang, Hanyang, Xingguo, Daye, and Qizhou, was rewarded with the rank of county assistant magistrate, and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took part in pacifying Yuezhou and helped capture Wuchang, Hanyang, Xingguo, Daye, and Qizhou; he was rewarded with the rank of county assistant magistrate and then promoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 五年，廣東賊犯湖南，湘撫駱秉章檄啟江募兵協剿，曰果字營，自是獨將一軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Guangdong rebels invaded Hunan, Hunan governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Qijiang to raise troops for coordinated suppression; the unit was called the Guozi Battalion, and from then on he alone commanded an army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, when rebels from Guangdong invaded Hunan, Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Qijiang to raise troops for the joint campaign; his command was called the Guozi Battalion, and from that point he led an army of his own.

sentences.zh: 攻茶陵踞匪，率壯士數十人薄南門，賊自民廛躍出，攢矛環刺，啟江手擒數賊，賊莫敢逼。

translations.literal: Attacking the bandits entrenched at Chaling, he led several dozen stalwarts to press close to the south gate; rebels leapt out from among the houses, massed spears and surrounded him with thrusts, yet Qijiang seized several rebels with his own hands and the rebels did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: When he attacked the rebels holding Chaling, he led several dozen picked men up to the south gate; rebels sprang out from the lanes, ringed him with spears, yet Qijiang seized several of them himself and none dared close on him.

sentences.zh: 尋會克其城，賊走江西，陷弋陽、興安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the city was taken in concert; the rebels fled into Jiangxi and captured Yiyang and Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: The city was soon taken in a combined assault; the rebels fled into Jiangxi and seized Yiyang and Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 啟江偕羅澤南复兩城，進收廣信，賜花翎，擢同知。

translations.literal: Qijiang together with Luo Zexi recovered the two cities, advanced to recover Guangxin, was granted the peacock feather, and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang and Luo Zexi recovered both cities, then advanced to retake Guangxin; he was awarded the peacock feather and promoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉長佑援江西，總統諸軍，啟江屬焉，駐師瀏陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liu Changyou came to aid Jiangxi as commander-in-chief of all forces; Qijiang was subordinate to him and encamped at Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 Liu Changyou marched to relieve Jiangxi as overall commander; Qijiang served under him and stationed his troops at Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 賊陷萬載，啟江大破之櫧樹潭、大橋、竹阜，遂復萬載；

translations.literal: When rebels seized Wanzai, Qijiang routed them at Zhushutan, Daqiao, and Zhufu, and thus recovered Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: After rebels took Wanzai, Qijiang routed them at Zhushutan, Daqiao, and Zhufu and recovered the county.

sentences.zh: 而崇通賊复犯瀏陽，援賊大至，撲營，啟江鏖戰敗之，躡至八角亭，毀其壘。

translations.literal: Then rebels from Chongyang and Tongcheng again invaded Liuyang; relief forces came in great numbers and stormed the camps, but Qijiang fought fiercely and defeated them, pursued to Bajiaoting, and destroyed their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Chongyang and Tongcheng then struck Liuyang again; large relief columns assaulted the camps, but Qijiang fought them off, pursued to Bajiaoting, and destroyed their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 會曾國華馳至，偕由洪塘、新昌、上高搗瑞州。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guohua arrived in haste, together they struck toward Ruizhou by way of Hongtang, Xinchang, and Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guohua then arrived in haste, and together they thrust toward Ruizhou by way of Hongtang, Xinchang, and Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 前軍至登龍橋，擊退袁州賊，進攻新昌、上高，拔之，擢知府。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Denglong Bridge, repelled the Yuanzhou rebels, advanced to attack Xinchang and Shanggao, took them, and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard reached Denglong Bridge, drove off the Yuanzhou rebels, and captured Xinchang and Shanggao; Qijiang was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 進攻袁州，啟江與長佑分地扼賊。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Yuanzhou, Qijiang and Changyou divided the ground to block the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As they pressed the attack on Yuanzhou, Qijiang and Changyou divided the approaches to hem in the rebels.

sentences.zh: 長佑攻西南，啟江攻東北，盡平城外賊屯。

translations.literal: Changyou attacked from the southwest and Qijiang from the northeast, leveling all rebel camps outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Changyou struck from the southwest while Qijiang struck from the northeast, clearing every rebel encampment outside the city.

sentences.zh: 城賊惶懼，啟江策臨吉賊必來援，設伏敗之，盡奪其輜重。

translations.literal: The rebels in the city were alarmed; Qijiang judged that rebels from Linji would certainly come to their aid, set an ambush and defeated them, and seized all their baggage and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison grew fearful; Qijiang predicted that Linji rebels would come to relieve them, ambushed the relief force, and captured all their supplies.

sentences.zh: 尋破賊合山，克分宜，加道銜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he broke the rebels at Heshan, captured Fenyi, and was given the rank of circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon routed the rebels at Heshan, took Fenyi, and was given the rank of circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 進攻臨江，七年正月，大捷陰岡嶺，斬其酋。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Linjiang, in the first month of the seventh year he won a great victory at Yingang Ridge and beheaded their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the attack on Linjiang, in the first month of 1857 he won a great victory at Yingang Ridge and killed their leader.

sentences.zh: 賊勢以孤，乃潛約撫、建、新淦援賊趨太平墟，犯長佑營。

translations.literal: As rebel strength grew isolated, they secretly summoned relief forces from Fuzhou, Jian, and Xin'gan to advance on Taipingxu and attack Changyou's camp.
translations.idiomatic: With their position growing desperate, the rebels secretly called in reinforcements from Fuzhou, Jian, and Xin'gan to strike at Taipingxu and assault Changyou's camp.

sentences.zh: 長佑戰失利，營陷，賊乘勢回犯陰岡嶺。

translations.literal: Changyou was defeated in battle and his camp fell; the rebels seized the momentum and turned back to attack Yingang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Changyou was beaten and his camp overrun; the rebels then swung back against Yingang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 部將田興恕、楊恆升突陣，斬悍酋數人，師從之，賊崩潰，夷其壘四十七。

translations.literal: His subordinates Tian Xingshu and Yang Hengsheng broke through the enemy line and beheaded several fierce chieftains; the army followed them, the rebels collapsed, and forty-seven stockades were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates Tian Xingshu and Yang Hengsheng charged the enemy line and killed several of their boldest leaders; the main force followed, the rebels broke, and forty-seven stockades were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 城賊窮蹙乞降，而賊首仍負嵎死拒，乃誘其出戰，啟江揮軍疾進，薄城而登，遂克之，擢道員，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The rebels in the city, pressed to extremity, begged to surrender, yet their leader still held the corner and resisted to the death; they therefore lured him out to battle, Qijiang waved the army forward in swift advance, pressed close to the wall and scaled it, and thus took the city; he was promoted to circuit commissioner and given the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison, cornered, asked to surrender, but their leader still fought from the walls; they lured him out, Qijiang drove his men forward at once, closed on the wall and scaled it, and took the city; he was promoted to circuit commissioner with the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長佑尋以病歸，劉坤一代之。

translations.literal: Changyou soon returned home on account of illness, and Liu Kunyi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Changyou soon went home ill, and Liu Kunyi took his place.

sentences.zh: 啟江與進攻撫州，連下宜黃、崇仁。

translations.literal: Qijiang advanced with him to attack Fuzhou and in succession took Yihuang and Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang joined the advance on Fuzhou and in succession captured Yihuang and Chongren.

sentences.zh: 撫州賊屯樟樹鎮，將伺官軍渡贛襲臨江，啟江與坤一回擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Fuzhou rebels were encamped at Zhangshu Town, intending to wait until the government army crossed the Gan to strike at Linjiang; Qijiang and Kunyi turned back and struck them, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels at Fuzhou held Zhangshu Town, planning to hit Linjiang once government troops crossed the Gan; Qijiang and Kunyi wheeled back and routed them.

sentences.zh: 進次上頓，距撫州十五里，築壘甫畢，賊至，迎擊敗之。

translations.literal: He advanced and halted at Shangdun, fifteen li from Fuzhou; the stockades had only just been built when rebels arrived, and he met them and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to Shangdun, fifteen li from Fuzhou; his fortifications were barely finished when rebels came up, and he met and beat them.

sentences.zh: 進攻高橋，賊棄城遁，追斬千七百有奇。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Gaoqiao, the rebels abandoned the city and fled; in pursuit more than seventeen hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the attack on Gaoqiao, he drove the rebels from the town; the pursuit left more than seventeen hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 撫州复，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Fuzhou was recovered, and he was given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou was recovered, and he received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，賊陷南安，糾眾數万犯贛州，踞新城墟及池江諸地。

translations.literal: In the ninth year rebels seized Nan'an, gathered forces in the tens of thousands to attack Ganzhou, and held Xinchengxu and the lands around Chijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 rebels took Nan'an, mustered tens of thousands against Ganzhou, and held Xinchengxu and the Chijiang region.

sentences.zh: 時曾國籓督援浙軍，啟江率所部從，檄援贛州。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Guofan was supervising the army sent to aid Zhejiang; Qijiang led his own troops in his train and was ordered to relieve Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was then directing the force sent to aid Zhejiang; Qijiang marched with his division and was ordered to relieve Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 啟江遣田勇三千誘賊，賊爭出赴利，啟江摧鋒直進，斬級數千。

translations.literal: Qijiang sent three thousand tianyong to lure the rebels; the rebels all rushed out for gain, and Qijiang drove the vanguard straight forward and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang sent three thousand local militiamen as bait; the rebels poured out after easy loot, and he drove the vanguard forward and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 田勇者，江西募農夫防賊，貪鹵獲，倚湘軍無所畏，集者四萬。

translations.literal: Tianyong were farmers recruited in Jiangxi to guard against rebels; greedy for booty and relying on the Hunan army without fear, forty thousand had gathered.
translations.idiomatic: These tianyong were Jiangxi farmers raised against the rebels; greedy for plunder and emboldened by the Hunan army, they had swelled to forty thousand.

sentences.zh: 啟江曰：「眾而不整必敗。

translations.literal: Qijiang said: "A multitude without discipline is sure to be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang said, "Numbers without order are doomed to defeat."

sentences.zh: 」禁之不可，遇伏果潰。

translations.literal: He could not forbid them; they met an ambush and indeed collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He could not restrain them; they walked into an ambush and broke.

sentences.zh: 湘軍為少卻，部將胡中和力戰斷後，復進敗之，平新城墟、池江、小溪、鳳凰城諸賊壘，賊退入南安。

translations.literal: The Hunan army was somewhat forced back; his subordinate Hu Zhonghe fought fiercely to cover the rear, then advanced again and defeated them, leveling the rebel stockades at Xinchengxu, Chijiang, Xiaoxi, and Fenghuangcheng; the rebels withdrew into Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan troops gave ground briefly; subordinate Hu Zhonghe fought a rear-guard action, then pressed forward again, took the rebel camps at Xinchengxu, Chijiang, Xiaoxi, and Fenghuangcheng, and drove the rebels back into Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 南安故有二城夾水，賊分屯相犄角，軍至皆棄而走。

translations.literal: Nan'an originally had two cities on either side of the water; the rebels were divided in garrison in mutual support, but when the army arrived they all abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an had long had twin towns on either bank; the rebels held both in mutual support, but at the army's approach they abandoned both and fled.

sentences.zh: 啟江進屯城外青隴、黃隴，結壘自固，令曰：「入城者斬。

translations.literal: Qijiang advanced and encamped outside the city at Qinglong and Huanglong, built stockades to secure himself, and issued the order: "Whoever enters the city shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang encamped outside at Qinglong and Huanglong, fortified his position, and ordered, "Anyone who enters the city will be executed."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，賊果還南城，攻之，敗走。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels indeed returned to the south city; he attacked them and they were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels did return to the south town; he attacked and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 啟江曰：「賊狡而弱，吾直驅之耳！

translations.literal: Qijiang said: "The rebels are cunning but weak; I shall simply drive straight at them!"
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang said, "They are tricky but feeble—we need only press them hard!"

sentences.zh: 」攀堞以登，賊奪西門走，追殺數十里，賜號額埒斯圖巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He scaled the parapet and mounted the wall; the rebels seized the west gate and fled; pursuit killed them for several tens of li; he was granted the title Elesitu Babaturu.
translations.idiomatic: He went up the battlements and over the wall; the rebels bolted through the west gate; the pursuit ran them down for miles; he was granted the title Elesitu Babaturu.

sentences.zh: 進信豐，會總兵遮克敦布攻吳家嶺，啟江率中營進。

translations.literal: He advanced to Xinfeng, joined the brigade-general Zhaketunbu in attacking Wujialing, and Qijiang led the central battalion forward.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on Xinfeng, joined Brigadier-General Zhaketunbu at Wujialing, and led the central battalion forward.

sentences.zh: 賊萬餘來撲，擊敗之，破先溪橋賊壘，城兵出而夾擊，立解其圍。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand rebels came to storm them; he defeated them, broke the rebel stockade at Xianxi Bridge, the garrison troops sallied out and struck from both sides, and the siege was at once relieved.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand rebels assailed them; he beat them off, took the camp at Xianxi Bridge, and with the garrison sallying out in concert broke the siege at once.

sentences.zh: 時江西郡縣皆复。

translations.literal: At that time all prefectures and counties of Jiangxi had been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By then every prefecture and county in Jiangxi had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 石達開由崇義竄湖南，郴、桂所屬皆告警，啟江馳防。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled from Chongyi into Hunan; all districts under Chen and Gui raised alarms, and Qijiang hurried to defend them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai broke out of Chongyi into Hunan; the Chenzhou and Guilin districts were all alarmed, and Qijiang rushed to the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊已由永州竄圍寶慶，啟江自臨、藍趨永州，扼東安，屯白牙市。

translations.literal: The rebels had already fled from Yongzhou to besiege Baojiang; Qijiang marched from Linwu and Lanshan toward Yongzhou, blocked Dong'an, and encamped at Baiyashi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already slipped from Yongzhou to besiege Shaoyang; Qijiang marched from Linwu and Lanshan toward Yongzhou, blocked Dong'an, and encamped at Baiyashi.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑、李續宜解寶慶圍，追至白牙，啟江會軍夾擊，擒其酋楊家廷、馬繼昌於陣。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou and Li Xuyi relieved the siege of Baojiang and pursued to Baiya; Qijiang joined the armies in a pincer attack and captured their chieftains Yang Jiating and Ma Jichang in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou and Li Xuyi lifted the siege of Shaoyang and pursued to Baiya; Qijiang joined in a converging attack and took their leaders Yang Jiating and Ma Jichang on the field.

sentences.zh: 賊竄入廣西，陷興安，盡集悍黨大溶江遏追師，遣別賊直犯桂林。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into Guangxi, seized Xing'an, gathered all their fierce bands at Darong River to block the pursuing army, and sent a separate force straight to assault Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Guangxi, took Xing'an, massed their hard fighters at Darong River to block pursuit, and sent another column straight at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 啟江由全州趨興安，復其城；

translations.literal: Qijiang marched from Quanzhou toward Xing'an and recovered its city.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang marched from Quanzhou to Xing'an and recovered the town.

sentences.zh: 攻大溶江，大捷，解桂林圍，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: He attacked Darong River, won a great victory, relieved the siege of Guilin, and was placed on the register for provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked at Darong River, won a great victory, relieved Guilin, and was placed on the register for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 移軍回湖南。

translations.literal: He moved his army back to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought his army back to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 四川軍事急，命啟江率師往援。

translations.literal: The military situation in Sichuan was urgent, and he was ordered to lead his army to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: With the fighting in Sichuan growing desperate, he was ordered to lead his troops there.

sentences.zh: 十年春，甫至，以疾卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, having only just arrived, he died of illness in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1860 he had barely arrived when he died of illness in camp.

sentences.zh: 詔贈巡撫，從優賜卹，諡壯果，湖南、江西並建專祠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of governor, gave preferential mourning compensation, and conferred the posthumous title Zhuangguo; dedicated shrines were built in both Hunan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted him governor's rank, generous compensation for his family, and the posthumous title Zhuangguo; dedicated shrines were raised in Hunan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 其所部留四川，駱秉章用以平賊焉。

translations.literal: His troops remained in Sichuan, and Luo Bingzhang used them to pacify the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His division remained in Sichuan, where Luo Bingzhang used it to finish pacifying the rebels.

sentences.zh: 張運蘭，字凱章，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunlan, styled Kaizhang, was a man of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunlan, whose courtesy name was Kaizhang, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從王珍轉戰衡、永、郴、桂，積功擢同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he followed Wang Zhen in campaigns through Heng, Yong, Chen, and Gui, and through accumulated merit was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he campaigned with Wang Zhen through Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guilin, and rose to subprefect on accumulated merit.

sentences.zh: 六年，戰通城，運蘭設三伏，營前斬賊酋張庸忠，擒魯三元，克通城，又大破賊於崇陽白蜺橋，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he fought at Tongcheng; Yunlan set three ambushes, beheaded the rebel chieftain Zhang Yongzhong before the camp, captured Lu Sanyuan, took Tongcheng, and again inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Baihong Bridge in Chongyang; he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he fought at Tongcheng; Yunlan laid three ambushes, killed rebel leader Zhang Yongzhong before the camp, captured Lu Sanyuan, and took the city; he then routed the rebels again at Baihong Bridge in Chongyang and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 七年，從王珍援江西，迭捷於臨江、吉安、樂安、新城、廣昌，功皆最。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Wang Zhen to aid Jiangxi and won repeated victories at Linjiang, Ji'an, Le'an, Xincheng, and Guangchang; his merit was foremost in all.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he followed Wang Zhen to Jiangxi and won victory after victory at Linjiang, Ji'an, Le'an, Xincheng, and Guangchang; his service ranked first throughout.

sentences.zh: 王珍卒於軍，運蘭與王開化分領其眾。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen died in the army; Yunlan and Wang Kaihua divided command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen died in camp, Yunlan and Wang Kaihua split command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 吉安賊窺永豐，運蘭屢敗之，擢知府。

translations.literal: Ji'an rebels watched for an opening at Yongfeng; Yunlan repeatedly defeated them and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an rebels probed Yongfeng; Yunlan beat them back again and again and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 又破賊於峽江橋阜灘、獅子山。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Qiaofutan and Shizishan in Xiajiang.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Qiaofutan and Shizishan on the Xiajiang.

sentences.zh: 移軍吉水，扼賊三曲灘，相持數日，血戰十數次，斬賊渠黃錫昆。

translations.literal: He moved his army to Jishui and blocked the rebels at Sanqu Beach; they faced each other for several days, fought bloody battles more than ten times, and beheaded the rebel leader Huang Xikun.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Jishui and blocked the rebels at Sanqu Beach; after several days and more than ten bloody clashes he killed their leader Huang Xikun.

sentences.zh: 渡贛江，破石達開於硃山橋，達開焚屯而遁，遂解永豐圍，擢道員。

translations.literal: Crossing the Gan River, he defeated Shi Dakai at Zhushan Bridge; Dakai burned his camps and fled, and the siege of Yongfeng was thus relieved; Yunlan was promoted to circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Gan, he routed Shi Dakai at Zhushan Bridge; Dakai burned his camps and fled, Yongfeng was relieved, and Yunlan was promoted to circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，略定樂安、宜黃，逼建昌，敗賊於厚坪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he largely pacified Le'an and Yihuang, pressed Jianchang, and defeated rebels at Houping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he largely secured Le'an and Yihuang, pressed Jianchang, and beat the rebels at Houping.

sentences.zh: 破水南賊巢，分剿南源、里塔墟、劉家坑，直搗謝坑，毀賊壘，斬其酋廖雄篙等，复南豐。

translations.literal: He broke the rebel nest south of the river, divided forces to suppress Nanyuan, Litaxu, and Liujiakeng, struck straight at Xiekeng, destroyed rebel stockades, beheaded their chieftains Liao Xionggao and others, and recovered Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed the rebel base south of the river, sent columns against Nanyuan, Litaxu, and Liujiakeng, drove straight to Xiekeng, destroyed their camps, killed leaders including Liao Xionggao, and recovered Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 建昌之圍始合，五月，克之，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The encirclement of Jianchang was at last closed; in the fifth month it was taken, and he was given the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The ring around Jianchang was finally closed; in the fifth month the city fell, and he received the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊复犯南豐，擊走之，追及新城杭山，降賊眾數千。

translations.literal: Rebels again invaded Nanfeng; he drove them off, pursued to Hangshan in Xincheng, and several thousand rebels surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck Nanfeng again he drove them off, pursued to Hangshan in Xincheng, and accepted the surrender of several thousand.

sentences.zh: 時詔起曾國籓督師規浙江，國籓行次江西，賊已入閩，疏調運蘭及蕭啟江率所部從。

translations.literal: At that time an edict recalled Zeng Guofan to command the army planning for Zhejiang; as Guofan passed through Jiangxi the rebels had already entered Fujian, and he memorialized to transfer Yunlan and Xiao Qijiang with their troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then recalled Zeng Guofan to take command of operations toward Zhejiang; passing through Jiangxi, he found the rebels already in Fujian and requested Yunlan and Xiao Qijiang with their divisions.

sentences.zh: 會賊陷安仁，別將失利，運蘭進擊，大破之，殲賊數千，克安仁，賜號克圖格爾依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When rebels seized Anren and another commander was defeated, Yunlan advanced to attack, inflicted a great defeat, destroyed several thousand rebels, took Anren, and was granted the title Ketuergeyi Babaturu.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels took Anren and another column was beaten, Yunlan attacked, routed them, killed several thousand, recovered Anren, and was granted the title Ketuergeyi Babaturu.

sentences.zh: 由杉關進剿破賊順昌，回援景德鎮，戰於李村，斬馘二千餘，解散千計。

translations.literal: Advancing through Shanguan to suppress rebels, he defeated them at Shunchang, returned to relieve Jingdezhen, fought at Licun, killed and captured more than two thousand, and disbanded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced through Shanguan, routed the rebels at Shunchang, turned back to relieve Jingdezhen, fought at Licun, killed or captured more than two thousand, and dispersed another thousand.

sentences.zh: 九年，援饒州，敗賊於栗樹山，克浮梁，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he relieved Raozhou, defeated rebels at Lishushan, took Fuliang, and was given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he relieved Raozhou, beat the rebels at Lishushan, took Fuliang, and received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，粵匪犯湖南寶慶，運蘭回援，疊破賊於宜章、星子、市禾洞，追至廣東連州，破九陂、石塘、白虎墟賊巢，殄賊逾萬，授開歸陳許道。

translations.literal: That autumn Guangdong rebels invaded Baojiang in Hunan; Yunlan returned to aid, repeatedly defeated rebels at Yizhang, Xingzi, and Shihedong, pursued to Lianzhou in Guangdong, broke rebel nests at Jiupi, Shitang, and Baihuxu, destroyed more than ten thousand rebels, and was appointed intendant of the Kaifeng-Guide-Chen-Xu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Guangdong rebels struck Shaoyang in Hunan; Yunlan marched back, beat them repeatedly at Yizhang, Xingzi, and Shihedong, pursued into Lianzhou in Guangdong, destroyed camps at Jiupi, Shitang, and Baihuxu, killed more than ten thousand rebels, and was appointed intendant of the Kaifeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國籓軍祁門，運蘭偕鮑超破賊黟、歙。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zeng Guofan's army was at Qimen; Yunlan together with Bao Chao defeated rebels in Yi and She.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, with Zeng Guofan's headquarters at Qimen, Yunlan and Bao Chao drove the rebels from Yi and She counties.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克休寧，擢福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he took Xiuning and was promoted to Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he took Xiuning and was promoted to Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再复黟縣，盡夷賊壘。

translations.literal: He again recovered Yi County and leveled all rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Yi County again and destroyed every rebel fort.

sentences.zh: 時運蘭統五千人防徽州，尋移防寧國，值大疫，悍賊麕集，與霆軍力拒之。

translations.literal: At that time Yunlan commanded five thousand men to defend Huizhou; soon he shifted to defend Ningguo; a great epidemic struck, fierce rebels gathered thickly, and together with the Ting Army he resisted them with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded five thousand men defending Huizhou, soon shifted to Ningguo, met a severe epidemic and masses of hard fighters, and with Bao Chao's Ting Army held them off.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，拔旌德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he took Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he captured Jingde.

sentences.zh: 二年，命援廣東，搗陽山石塋賊巢，降其眾三千，擒巨酋李復猷於連州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was ordered to aid Guangdong, stormed the rebel nest at Shidang in Yangshan, accepted the surrender of three thousand of their followers, and captured the great chieftain Li Fuyou at Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was sent to aid Guangdong, stormed the rebel stronghold at Shidang in Yangshan, accepted three thousand surrenders, and captured the great leader Li Fuyou at Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，赴福建按察使任。

translations.literal: In the third year he went to take up his post as Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he went to take up his post as Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時江、浙逸賊眾猶十餘萬，由江西入閩，蹂汀、漳二郡。

translations.literal: At that time remnant rebels in Jiangsu and Zhejiang still numbered more than a hundred thousand; entering Fujian from Jiangxi, they ravaged the two prefectures of Ting and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant rebels in Jiangsu and Zhejiang still numbered over a hundred thousand; pouring into Fujian from Jiangxi, they ravaged Ting and Zhang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 運蘭率五百人趨武平，遇賊，眾寡不敵，總兵賀世楨、王明高，副將雷照雄皆戰歿；

translations.literal: Yunlan led five hundred men in haste to Wuping, met the rebels, and was outnumbered; brigade-generals He Shizhen and Wang Minggao and vice-commandant Lei Zhaoxiong all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlan rushed to Wuping with five hundred men, met the rebels at hopeless odds, and brigadiers He Shizhen and Wang Minggao and vice-commandant Lei Zhaoxiong were all killed.

sentences.zh: 運蘭被執，罵賊，支解之。

translations.literal: Yunlan was captured, cursed the rebels, and was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlan was taken, cursed his captors, and was cut to pieces.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈巡撫，予騎都尉世職，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted the rank of governor, given the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry, and conferred the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he was posthumously made governor, granted a hereditary commandant's rank, and given the posthumous title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 武平及湖南、廣東建專祠。

translations.literal: Dedicated shrines were built at Wuping and in Hunan and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated shrines were raised at Wuping and in Hunan and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 唐訓方，字義渠，湖南常寧人。

translations.literal: Tang Xunfang, styled Yiqu, was a man of Changning in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xunfang, whose courtesy name was Yiqu, came from Changning in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年舉人，大挑教諭。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination and in the great selection was appointed instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in 1840 and in the great selection was appointed a district instructor.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，曾國籓創水師，訓方領副右營，嗣改入陸軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, when Zeng Guofan created the naval force, Xunfang commanded the Right Rear Battalion; afterward he was transferred to the land army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, when Zeng Guofan formed the river force, Xunfang led the Right Rear Battalion; he was later transferred to the land army.

sentences.zh: 從羅澤南克蒲圻，复武昌，又從攻興國金牛堡。

translations.literal: He followed Luo Zexi in capturing Puqi, recovering Wuchang, and again followed in the attack on the Jiniu Fortress in Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Luo Zexi in taking Puqi and recovering Wuchang, then joined the assault on Jiniu Fortress in Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 國籓命募常寧勇五百人統之，曰訓字營。

translations.literal: Guofan ordered him to raise five hundred Changning braves to command; the unit was called the Xunzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan had him raise five hundred men from Changning; his command was called the Xunzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 從克田家鎮、蘄州、廣濟，拔黃梅，進軍濯港，敗悍酋羅大綱。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Tianjiazhen, Qizhou, and Guangji, took Huangmei, advanced to Zhuogang, and defeated the fierce chieftain Luo Dagang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Tianjiazhen, Qizhou, and Guangji, captured Huangmei, advanced to Zhuogang, and defeated the fierce leader Luo Dagang.

sentences.zh: 是夕，賊謀襲大營，訓方巡營驚覺，賊退走。

translations.literal: That night the rebels plotted to raid the main camp; Xunfang on patrol was alerted, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebels planned a raid on headquarters; Xunfang on patrol detected them and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日，攻孔壟街口，訓方率壯士踏肩陟高墉，諸軍乘之，遂破孔壟。

translations.literal: The next day, attacking the Konglong street entrance, Xunfang led stalwarts who stepped on one another's shoulders to climb the high wall; the armies followed them and thus broke Konglong.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, assaulting the Konglong gate, Xunfang led men up the high wall on one another's shoulders; the rest of the army followed and Konglong fell.

sentences.zh: 五年，從澤南援江西，克弋陽、興安、廣信、德興、浮梁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zexi to aid Jiangxi and captured Yiyang, Xing'an, Guangxin, Dexing, and Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he followed Zexi to Jiangxi and took Yiyang, Xing'an, Guangxin, Dexing, and Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 援義寧賊屯城外雞鳴、鳳凰二山，與城犄角。

translations.literal: Relieving Yining, rebels were encamped outside the city on Jiming and Fenghuang mountains, supporting the city in mutual defense.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving Yining, he found rebels on Jiming and Fenghuang hills outside the walls, holding the city in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 訓方逼雞鳴山下，督隊先登，賊驚潰，乘勝拔其城。

translations.literal: Xunfang pressed to the foot of Jiming Mountain, urged his men to climb first, the rebels fled in alarm, and seizing the victory he took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xunfang pressed Jiming Hill, drove his men up first, routed the rebels, and pressed on to take the city.

sentences.zh: 從澤南援武漢，克蒲圻，進攻武昌。

translations.literal: He followed Zexi to aid Wuhan, captured Puqi, and advanced to attack Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zexi to relieve Wuhan, retook Puqi, and advanced on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 累擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to prefect and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to prefect and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，率三百人夜由鮎魚套至藕塘，奪二壘，又破援賊於豹子海。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he led three hundred men by night from Nianyu Bay to Outang, seized two stockades, and again defeated relief rebels at Baozihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1856 he led three hundred men by night from Nianyu Bay to Outang, took two stockades, and routed relief forces at Baozihai.

sentences.zh: 會襄陽土匪高二倡亂，圍府城，巡撫胡林翼令訓方偕舒保馬隊往剿。

translations.literal: When bandits led by Gao Erchang rose in Xiangyang and besieged the prefectural city, Governor Hu Linyi ordered Xunfang to go with Shu Bao's cavalry to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Erchang's bandits rebelled at Xiangyang and besieged the prefectural seat, Governor Hu Linyi sent Xunfang with Shu Bao's cavalry to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 破賊於峪山，援賊至，又敗之。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels at Yushan; relief rebels arrived and he defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them at Yushan; when reinforcements came he beat them again.

sentences.zh: 進克樊城，追至呂堰驛，斬女賊宋氏。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Fancheng, pursued to Luyan Post, and beheaded the female rebel Song.
translations.idiomatic: He took Fancheng, pursued to Luyan Post, and killed the female rebel leader Song.

sentences.zh: 援宜昌，破賊於南漳，權襄陽知府。

translations.literal: He relieved Yichang, defeated rebels at Nanzhang, and acted as prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Yichang, routed rebels at Nanzhang, and served as acting prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，川匪劉尚義犯宜城，揚言趨荊門，而使南漳賊襲府城，訓方備之，急扼武安堰，賊奔據武安城，進攻之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year Sichuan rebels under Liu Shangyi invaded Yicheng, claiming they would march on Jingmen while sending Nanzhang rebels to raid the prefectural city; Xunfang prepared against them, hurried to block Wu'an Weir, the rebels fled to hold Wu'an City, and he advanced to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1857 Liu Shangyi's Sichuan rebels struck Yicheng, claiming a move on Jingmen while Nanzhang rebels hit the prefectural seat; Xunfang blocked Wu'an Weir, drove the rebels into Wu'an City, and attacked.

sentences.zh: 會都統巴揚阿來招降，訓方進剿高二於璩灣，乘雪夜進攻，擒之；

translations.literal: When Commander-in-chief Bayang'a came to accept surrenders, Xunfang advanced to suppress Gao Er at Quwan, attacked on a snowy night, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander-in-chief Bayang'a arrived to accept surrenders, Xunfang pressed Gao Er at Quwan, attacked on a snowy night, and took him.

sentences.zh: 而巴揚阿所撫賊复叛，掠鄖、房、保山、竹山、竹谿、保康、興山。

translations.literal: But the rebels Bayang'a had pacified rebelled again and plundered Yun, Fang, Baoshan, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Baokang, and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: But rebels Bayang'a had pacified rose again and ravaged Yun, Fang, Baoshan, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Baokang, and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 訓方會陝西軍連破之武當山金頂，斬其渠，餘賊降。

translations.literal: Xunfang joined Shaanxi troops in repeatedly defeating them at the Golden Summit of Wudang Mountain, beheaded their leader, and the remaining rebels surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xunfang joined Shaanxi troops, routed them repeatedly at the Golden Summit of Wudang Mountain, killed their leader, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 襄郡悉定。

translations.literal: The whole Xiangyang region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The whole Xiangyang region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 先以克武漢論功以道員記名，至是加按察使銜，授湖北督糧道。

translations.literal: Earlier, for merit in recovering Wuhan he had been placed on the register as circuit commissioner; now he was given the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and appointed grain transport commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been placed on the register as circuit commissioner for recovering Wuhan; now he received the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and was appointed Hubei's grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成合捻匪犯蘄、黃，訓方自襄陽赴援，連戰敗賊，進屯張家塝。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng together with Nian rebels invaded Qi and Huang; Xunfang came from Xiangyang to aid, repeatedly defeated the rebels in battle, and advanced to encamp at Zhangjiabang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng joined Nian rebels in striking Qizhou and Huangmei; Xunfang marched from Xiangyang, beat them in repeated fights, and encamped at Zhangjiabang.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼令於蘄州境內建碉卡，訓方以二千人守之，賊迭來攻，皆擊退，賜號奇齊葉勒特依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi ordered blockhouses built within Qizhou territory; Xunfang guarded them with two thousand men; rebels came to attack again and again and were all repelled; he was granted the title Qiqiyeleteyi Babaturu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi ordered blockhouses built in Qizhou; Xunfang held them with two thousand men and repelled every assault; he was granted the title Qiqiyeleteyi Babaturu.

sentences.zh: 調援臨淮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to relieve Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to relieve Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 尋以李續賓軍覆三河，回防湖北，屯陳德園。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, he returned to defend Hubei and encamped at Chendeyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, he returned to defend Hubei and encamped at Chendeyuan.

sentences.zh: 九年，會攻太湖，賊圍鮑超於小池驛，多隆阿不能救，令訓方移軍近鮑營為接應。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, in the joint attack on Taihu, rebels besieged Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post; Duolong'a could not save him and ordered Xunfang to move his army close to Bao's camp as support.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, during the attack on Taihu, rebels besieged Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post; Duolong'a could not relieve him and ordered Xunfang to move up near Bao's camp.

sentences.zh: 甫至，築壘未就，為賊所乘，乃退屯新倉。

translations.literal: He had only just arrived when his stockades were not yet finished and the rebels seized the opportunity; he therefore withdrew to encamp at Xincang.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely arrived when his fortifications were unfinished and the rebels struck; he fell back to Xincang.

sentences.zh: 十年，解軍事，赴糧道任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was released from military duties and went to take up the grain transport post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he left military service and took up the grain transport post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，連擢湖北布政使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted in succession to Hubei provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Hubei provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，胡林翼駐軍英山，病甚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Hu Linyi was stationed at Yingshan and was gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Hu Linyi lay gravely ill at Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 賊上犯黃州，抵灄口，武昌震動，訛言繁興。

translations.literal: Rebels advanced to invade Huangzhou and reached Shuankou; Wuchang was shaken and rumors flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels advanced on Huangzhou to Shuankou; Wuchang panicked and rumors spread.

sentences.zh: 訓方處以鎮靜，誅亂民數人，人心始定。

translations.literal: Xunfang handled matters with calm; he executed several disorderly civilians, and public sentiment at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xunfang kept calm, executed several troublemakers, and public order returned.

sentences.zh: 灄口賊亦擊退。

translations.literal: The rebels at Shuankou were also driven off.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Shuankou were also driven off.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，安徽巡撫李續宜因母喪奪情，請假回籍，舉訓方自代，命暫行署理。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Anhui governor Li Xuyi, retaining his post despite his mother's death, asked leave to return home and recommended Xunfang to replace him; he was ordered to act temporarily in the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Anhui Governor Li Xuyi, remaining in office despite mourning his mother, asked leave and recommended Xunfang as his replacement; Xunfang was ordered to act in the post.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖反側久，遂叛，安徽諸軍皆不能制。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin had long wavered and at last rebelled; none of the armies in Anhui could control him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Peilin, long wavering, finally rebelled, and no Anhui army could control him.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧格林沁大軍至，始平之。

translations.literal: In the second year the great army of Senggelinqin arrived and at last pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Senggelinqin's main force arrived and at last subdued him.

sentences.zh: 撫循降圩，收其兵械，奏移鳳臺，治下蔡雉河集，增立渦陽縣。

translations.literal: He soothed the surrendered stockades, collected their weapons, memorialized to move Fengtai, govern Xiaheji at Xiazai, and add the new county of Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified surrendered stockades, collected their arms, moved Fengtai, governed Xiaheji at Xiazai, and established the new county of Woyang.

sentences.zh: 都統富明阿奏劾訓方，降調。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Fuming'a memorialized to impeach Xunfang, and he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Fuming'a impeached Xunfang, and he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 三年，署湖北按察使，尋署巡撫，授直隸布政使，兼統練軍出省防剿。

translations.literal: In the third year he acted as Hubei provincial surveillance commissioner, soon acted as governor, was appointed Zhili provincial administration commissioner, and also commanded the training army in field defense outside the province.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he acted as Hubei surveillance commissioner, then as governor, was appointed Zhili administration commissioner, and led training troops on field duty beyond the province.

sentences.zh: 七年，西捻平。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 the Western Nian were pacified.

sentences.zh: 請開缺省墓。

translations.literal: He requested to vacate his post and return home to tend his parents' graves.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign and return home to tend his parents' graves.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1877.

sentences.zh: 湖北請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Hubei requested that he be enshrined in the temple of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei requested his enshrinement in the temple of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 蔣凝學，字之純，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Jiang Ningxue, styled Zhipure, was a man of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ningxue, whose courtesy name was Zhipure, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，在籍治鄉團。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, while still in his native place, he organized local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he organized local militia in his home district.

sentences.zh: 五年，從羅澤南克武昌，獎國子監典簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Luo Zexi in capturing Wuchang and was rewarded with the post of archivist of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he followed Luo Zexi in taking Wuchang and was rewarded with an Imperial Academy archivist post.

sentences.zh: 六年，率湘左兩營從巡撫胡林翼攻武昌。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led the two Xiang Left battalions with Governor Hu Linyi to attack Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he led the two Xiang Left battalions with Governor Hu Linyi against Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 屯賽湖堤，引江水入湖，合長圍，進薄城下，平賊壘十餘。

translations.literal: He encamped on the Saihu embankment, diverted river water into the lake, joined the long encirclement, advanced close beneath the walls, and leveled more than ten rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He camped on the Saihu embankment, diverted river water into the lake, joined the long siege, pressed to the walls, and destroyed more than ten rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 武昌复，論功擢知縣。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was recovered, he was promoted to county magistrate for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell he was promoted to county magistrate for merit.

sentences.zh: 從克黃州、大冶、興國，逼九江。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Huangzhou, Daye, and Xingguo, pressing Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Huangzhou, Daye, and Xingguo and pressed Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，分統三營屯北岸陸家嘴​​，攻小池口，屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he separately commanded three battalions encamped at Lujiazui on the north bank, attacked Xiaochikou, and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he commanded three battalions at Lujiazui on the north bank, attacked Xiaochikou, and won every fight.

sentences.zh: 都興阿檄攻童司簰。

translations.literal: Duxing'a ordered an attack on Tongsipai.
translations.idiomatic: Duxing'a ordered an attack on Tongsipai.

sentences.zh: 童司簰背江據湖，通黃梅要隘，賊五六萬踞之。

translations.literal: Tongsipai backed on the river and held the lake, communicating with the strategic pass of Huangmei; fifty or sixty thousand rebels occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Tongsipai lay between river and lake on the route to Huangmei, held by fifty or sixty thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 至則賊數搏戰，凝學堅持不退。

translations.literal: On arrival the rebels fought repeatedly, but Ningxue held firm and would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked again and again, but Ningxue held his ground.

sentences.zh: 尋陳玉成來援，眾議退兵，凝學曰：「童司簰不克，水師往來失所據，九江之師亦掣肘，勢所必爭。

translations.literal: Soon Chen Yucheng came to their aid; the assembly debated withdrawing, but Ningxue said: "If Tongsipai is not taken, the naval force loses its footing for coming and going, and the Jiujiang army is also hampered—this is ground that must be contested."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yucheng came to relieve them, many urged retreat; Ningxue said, "If we fail at Tongsipai the fleet loses its base and Jiujiang is hampered—we must fight for it."

sentences.zh: 」請增兵千人，宵濟合水師，連日鏖戰，破之，平賊壘數十，進克黃梅，擢同知。

translations.literal: He requested an additional thousand troops, crossed by night to join the naval force, fought fierce battles for successive days, broke them, leveled dozens of rebel stockades, advanced to take Huangmei, and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for another thousand men, crossed by night with the fleet, fought for days, broke the position, destroyed dozens of camps, took Huangmei, and was promoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，會攻九江府城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he joined the attack on the Jiujiang prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he joined the assault on Jiujiang city.

sentences.zh: 凝學穴地道迤東而南，地雷發，壞城垣百餘丈，從缺口入，殲賊甚眾，擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Ningxue dug a tunnel winding east and south; the land mine exploded, destroying more than a hundred zhang of wall; he entered through the breach and destroyed a great many rebels; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxue dug a tunnel east and south; the mine blew a hundred-zhang breach in the wall; he stormed through and killed many rebels; he was promoted to prefect and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 連复麻城、黃安，擢道員。

translations.literal: He recovered Macheng and Huang'an in succession and was promoted to circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Macheng and Huang'an in turn and was promoted to circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十月，李續賓三河軍覆，官文檄凝學間道遏剿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, when Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, Guanwen ordered Ningxue by a side route to intercept and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, when Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, Guanwen ordered Ningxue by a side route to intercept the rebels.

sentences.zh: 會多隆阿、鮑超擊賊於宿松花亭子，破之。

translations.literal: Duolong'a and Bao Chao together attacked the rebels at Songtingzi in Suzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Duolong'a and Bao Chao together routed the rebels at Songtingzi in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊退太湖、潛山，凝學駐防荊橋。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew to Taihu and Qianshan; Ningxue garrisoned Jingqiao.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Taihu and Qianshan; Ningxue garrisoned Jingqiao.

sentences.zh: 九年，移屯黃州羅田，會攻太湖。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he moved to encamp at Luotian in Huangzhou and joined the attack on Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he moved to Luotian in Huangzhou and joined the attack on Taihu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，陳​​玉成大舉來援，凝學移軍龍家涼亭，與鮑超小池驛之軍為犄角，留四營遏太湖東門，城賊出，擊退之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chen Yucheng came in force to aid them; Ningxue moved his army to Longjialiangting, supported Bao Chao's force at Xiaochi Post in mutual defense, left four battalions to block Taihu's east gate, and when garrison rebels sallied out he drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chen Yucheng came in force; Ningxue moved to Longjialiangting to support Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post, left four battalions at Taihu's east gate, and beat back a sally from the city.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，鮑營被圍急，凝學進援，甫拔營，賊大隊來抄，凝學揮軍截擊，多隆阿率馬隊應之，戰竟日，擒斬二千餘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year Bao's camp was urgently besieged; Ningxue advanced to aid, had only just raised the siege when a large rebel column came to outflank them; Ningxue waved his army to intercept, Duolong'a led the cavalry to respond, they fought all day, and captured or killed more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1860 Bao's camp was hard pressed; Ningxue relieved it, but a large rebel column then tried to cut them off; Ningxue intercepted, Duolong'a's cavalry joined in, and after a full day's fighting they killed or captured more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻羅山，衝賊壘，諸軍合擊，賊大潰，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: Seizing the victory he attacked Luoshan, charged the rebel stockades, the armies struck together, the rebels collapsed in great disorder, and he was given the nominal rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage he took Luoshan, stormed the rebel camps in concert with other columns, routed them completely, and received the nominal rank of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，陳玉成復犯湖北，凝學回援武昌縣，敗賊赤壁山下，復其城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chen Yucheng again invaded Hubei; Ningxue returned to aid Wuchang County, defeated the rebels below Chibi Mountain, and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Chen Yucheng invaded Hubei again; Ningxue marched back, routed the rebels below Chibi Mountain, and recovered Wuchang County.

sentences.zh: 會總兵成大吉等攻黃州數月不下，詔降賊目劉維楨，复蘄州，選出眾五百人為忠義營，使維楨詐稱援軍，誘城賊出，擊之，遂克黃州，以道員記名，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Brigade-general Cheng Daji and others had attacked Huangzhou for months without success; an edict accepted the surrender of the rebel officer Liu Weizhen; Qizhou was recovered; five hundred picked men were chosen for the Zhongyi Battalion; Liu Weizhen was made to feign relief troops, lure the city rebels out, and strike them; Huangzhou was thus taken; Ningxue was placed on the register as circuit commissioner and given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier Cheng Daji had besieged Huangzhou for months in vain; the court accepted rebel officer Liu Weizhen's surrender, recovered Qizhou, formed five hundred picked men into the Zhongyi Battalion, had Liu feign a relief column to lure the garrison out, and took Huangzhou; Ningxue was placed on the register as circuit commissioner with the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖叛，陷壽州，凝學進屯六安，克霍丘，增募水陸軍。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin rebelled and seized Shouzhou; Ningxue advanced to encamp at Lu'an, took Huoqiu, and increased recruitment for land and river forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Peilin rebelled and took Shouzhou, Ningxue advanced to Lu'an, captured Huoqiu, and enlarged his land and river forces.

sentences.zh: 苗黨姚有志、潘塏等乞降，各圩多反正，授甘肅安肅道。

translations.literal: Miao partisans Yao Youzhi, Pan Kai, and others begged to surrender; many stockades returned to allegiance; he was appointed intendant of the Ansu circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao followers Yao Youzhi and Pan Kai surrendered; many stockades returned to allegiance; he was appointed intendant of the Ansu circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，移屯潁州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he moved to encamp at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he moved his camp to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪李世賢北竄，凝學移軍舒城，擊敗之，又追敗之六安，賊引去。

translations.literal: In the second year Guangdong rebel Li Shixian fled north; Ningxue moved his army to Shucheng, defeated him, again defeated him in pursuit at Lu'an, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Li Shixian fled north; Ningxue moved to Shucheng, beat him, pursued and beat him again at Lu'an, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖复圍壽州，凝學回援，破賊於牛尾岡。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin again besieged Shouzhou; Ningxue returned to aid and defeated the rebels at Niuwei Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Peilin besieged Shouzhou again, Ningxue returned and routed him at Niuwei Ridge.

sentences.zh: 壽州尋陷，凝學坐救援不力，褫布政使銜，仍駐防潁州。

translations.literal: Shouzhou soon fell; Ningxue was punished for ineffective relief, stripped of his provincial administration commissioner rank, and still garrisoned Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou soon fell; Ningxue was blamed for slow relief, stripped of his administration commissioner's rank, and remained at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會僧格林沁督師剿沛霖，凝學克霍丘各圩，水師分駐三河尖、臨淮關，進破黃梁集，克潁上，收附近城各圩，斬賊黨苗呆和、苗呆花，复懷遠。

translations.literal: When Senggelinqin supervised the campaign against Peilin, Ningxue took the stockades around Huoqiu; the naval force was divided between Sanhejian and Linhuaiguan; he advanced to break Huangliangji, took Yingshang, recovered nearby walled towns and stockades, beheaded the Miao partisans Miao Daihe and Miao Daihua, and recovered Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Senggelinqin took command against Peilin, Ningxue took the Huoqiu stockades; his fleet held Sanhejian and Linhuaiguan; he broke Huangliangji, took Yingshang, recovered nearby towns and stockades, killed Miao Daihe and Miao Daihua, and recovered Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 沛霖勢日蹙，遂走死。

translations.literal: Peilin's position grew daily more desperate, and he fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin's position collapsed, and he fled to his death.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪陳得才等糾眾三十萬自陝西回竄，圖救江寧。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangdong rebels Chen Decai and others gathered three hundred thousand men fleeing back from Shaanxi, intending to relieve Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Chen Decai and other Guangdong rebels mustered three hundred thousand men fleeing back from Shaanxi to relieve Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 凝學屯英山，遏賊金家鋪，敗之。

translations.literal: Ningxue encamped at Yingshan, blocked the rebels at Jinjiapu, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxue camped at Yingshan, blocked them at Jinjiapu, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賊復自麻城犯霍山，凝學退石家嘴，與按察使英翰相犄角，伺賊過狙擊，殪千餘人，拔出難民數千。

translations.literal: The rebels again from Macheng invaded Huoshan; Ningxue withdrew to Shijiazui, supported Surveillance Commissioner Ying Han in mutual defense, waited for the rebels to pass and ambushed them, killed more than a thousand, and rescued several thousand refugees.
translations.idiomatic: They struck Huoshan again from Macheng; Ningxue fell back to Shijiazui, coordinated with Surveillance Commissioner Ying Han, ambushed the column, killed more than a thousand, and rescued several thousand civilians.

sentences.zh: 英山解嚴，复布政使銜。

translations.literal: The alarm at Yingshan was lifted, and he recovered his provincial administration commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis at Yingshan passed, he recovered his administration commissioner's rank.

sentences.zh: 進援湖北，收復羅田、蘄水、麻城三縣，解蔡家河圍。

translations.literal: He advanced to aid Hubei, recovered the three counties of Luotian, Qishui, and Macheng, and relieved the siege at Caijiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced into Hubei, recovered Luotian, Qishui, and Macheng, and lifted the siege at Caijiahe.

sentences.zh: 賊复竄安徽，凝學躡追，沿途襲擊，繞出賊前，遏之霍山長嶺庵。

translations.literal: The rebels again fled into Anhui; Ningxue pursued close behind, struck them along the way, swung ahead of them, and blocked them at Changling'an in Huoshan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled back into Anhui; Ningxue pursued, struck them along the route, swung ahead, and blocked them at Changling'an in Huoshan.

sentences.zh: 路險，賊不虞兵猝至，多墜澗死，降者三四萬，賊首陳得才仰藥死。

translations.literal: The road was perilous; the rebels did not expect troops to arrive so suddenly; many fell into ravines and died; thirty or forty thousand surrendered; the rebel leader Chen Decai took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the narrow road the rebels were caught unawares; many fell into ravines; thirty or forty thousand surrendered; Chen Decai took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 簡降眾為步隊五營、馬隊三營，餘悉遣散。

translations.literal: He selected the surrendered masses into five infantry battalions and three cavalry battalions, and dispersed all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He formed five infantry and three cavalry battalions from the surrendered ranks and discharged the rest.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，陝甘總督楊岳斌奏調凝學赴甘肅，行次樊城，會霆軍譁變。

translations.literal: That winter Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Yang Yuebin memorialized to transfer Ningxue to Gansu; on the way, passing Fancheng, the Ting Army mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Governor Yang Yuebin of Shaanxi and Gansu requested Ningxue for Gansu; passing Fancheng, Bao Chao's Ting Army mutinied.

sentences.zh: 凝學所部亦以欠餉不靖，請於巡撫鄭敦謹，借款資遣湘左八營，留忠義營於湖北，自請回籍養病。

translations.literal: Ningxue's own troops also grew restless for lack of pay; he requested Governor Zheng Dunjin to borrow funds to discharge the eight Xiang Left battalions, left the Zhongyi Battalion in Hubei, and asked to return home to recover from illness.
translations.idiomatic: His own troops also mutinied over unpaid wages; he borrowed from Governor Zheng Dunjin to discharge the eight Xiang Left battalions, left the Zhongyi Battalion in Hubei, and asked to go home to recover.

sentences.zh: 命兩月假滿仍赴甘肅。

translations.literal: He was ordered that when his two months' leave ended he should still proceed to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to proceed to Gansu when his two months' leave ended.

sentences.zh: 五年，募湘勇二千，號安字營。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he recruited two thousand Hunan braves, called the Anzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he raised two thousand Hunan braves as the Anzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 至西安，巡撫劉蓉奏請凝學屯涇州，兼顧關隴。

translations.literal: Reaching Xi'an, Governor Liu Rong memorialized requesting that Ningxue encamp at Jingzhou and also watch over Guan and Long.
translations.idiomatic: At Xi'an, Governor Liu Rong asked that he camp at Jingzhou and cover the Guanlong region.

sentences.zh: 六月，敗回匪於華亭，與提督雷正綰、總兵張在山等約夾擊，深入被圍，士卒死傷七百餘人，總兵周太和、周清貴，副將黃德太等均歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he defeated Muslim rebels at Huating; with Regional Commander Lei Zhengwan, Brigadier-General Zhang Zaishan, and others he agreed on a converging attack; advancing deep he was surrounded; more than seven hundred soldiers were killed or wounded; brigade-generals Zhou Taihe and Zhou Qinggui and vice-commandant Huang Detai all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he beat Muslim rebels at Huating; with Regional Commander Lei Zhengwan and Brigadier Zhang Zaishan he planned a pincer attack, advanced too far, was surrounded, lost more than seven hundred men, and brigadiers Zhou Taihe and Zhou Qinggui and vice-commandant Huang Detai were killed.

sentences.zh: 凝學潰圍出，屯平涼，轉戰而前，至省城，署蘭州道。

translations.literal: Ningxue broke out of the encirclement, encamped at Pingliang, fought forward in stages to the provincial capital, and acted as Lanzhou circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxue broke out, camped at Pingliang, fought forward to the provincial capital, and acted as Lanzhou intendant.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，回匪犯蘭州，守城兵僅凝學所部千餘人，登陴固守，屢出奇兵焚賊壘，賊尋退，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year Muslim rebels attacked Lanzhou; the garrison was only a little more than a thousand of Ningxue's troops; he mounted the walls and held firm, repeatedly sent surprise forces to burn rebel stockades, the rebels soon withdrew, and he was placed on the register for provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1867 Muslim rebels attacked Lanzhou; only a thousand-odd of Ningxue's men held the walls; he sent sorties to burn rebel camps until they withdrew; he was placed on the register for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he acted as provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，复署蘭州道，擢山西按察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again acted as Lanzhou circuit intendant and was promoted to Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he again acted as Lanzhou intendant and was promoted to Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，遷陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was transferred to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was transferred to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，以病解官，未行而卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he resigned on account of illness and died before he could depart.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he resigned for illness and died before he could leave office.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Mourning compensation was granted, and he was posthumously made a Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted compensation and posthumously made him a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 陳湜，字舫仙，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Chen Shi, styled Fangxian, was a man of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi, whose courtesy name was Fangxian, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，曾國荃赴援江西，招湜襄軍事，從克安福、萬安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Zeng Guoquan went to aid Jiangxi, recruited Shi to assist in military affairs, and followed in capturing Anfu and Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 Zeng Guoquan marched to Jiangxi, recruited Shi as his military aide, and took Anfu and Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 七年，進圍吉安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he advanced to besiege Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he advanced to besiege Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 國荃奔喪去軍，湜代領其眾。

translations.literal: Guoquan left the army to observe mourning for his father; Shi took command of his forces in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoquan left for his father's mourning, Shi took command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he too returned home on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned home for his own father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 八年，從蔣益澧援廣西，克平樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed Jiang Yizao to aid Guangxi and captured Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he followed Jiang Yizao to Guangxi and took Pingle.

sentences.zh: 賊趨桂林，湜率四營遏之於大灣車埠，敗之，乘勝劃蘇橋壘。

translations.literal: The rebels moved toward Guilin; Shi led four battalions to block them at Dawan Chebu, defeated them, and seizing the victory destroyed the stockade at Suqiao.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels moved on Guilin, Shi with four battalions blocked them at Dawan Chebu, routed them, and destroyed the camp at Suqiao.

sentences.zh: 從攻柳州，克潯州。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Liuzhou and captured Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the attack on Liuzhou and captured Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開圍寶慶，湜募千人出祁陽赴援，與李續宜夾擊破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baojiang; Shi recruited a thousand men, marched out from Qiyang to aid, and together with Li Xuyi struck from both sides and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 Shi Dakai besieged Shaoyang; Shi raised a thousand men from Qiyang, joined Li Xuyi in a converging attack, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國荃圍安慶，使湜總軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing and made Shi overall commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing and put Shi in charge of operations.

sentences.zh: 湜規地形，請堨樅陽口蓄水阻援賊，力扼集賢關，從之。

translations.literal: Shi surveyed the terrain, requested damming Zongyang Mouth to store water and block relief rebels, and strongly urged holding Jixian Pass; his plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi surveyed the ground, proposed damming Zongyang Mouth to hold back relief forces, and urged a tight hold on Jixian Pass; Guoquan agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊酋陳玉成來援，阻水，趨集賢關，擊破之。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Chen Yucheng came to aid them, was blocked by the water, moved toward Jixian Pass, and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Chen Yucheng came to relieve the city, was blocked by the water, struck at Jixian Pass, and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，自是獨領一軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was taken, and from then on he alone commanded an army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Anqing fell, and from then on he commanded an army of his own.

sentences.zh: 循江而東，會克諸城隘，累​​擢至道員。

translations.literal: He followed the river eastward, joined in capturing walled towns and passes, and through repeated promotions rose to circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He marched downriver, helped take towns and passes along the way, and rose step by step to circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從國荃攻江寧，建議先並力九洑洲，斷江北接濟，先後會諸軍擊走李秀成、李世賢援眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Guoquan in attacking Jiangning, proposed first concentrating force on Jiufuzhou to cut off relief from north of the river, and in succession joined the armies in driving off the relief forces of Li Xiucheng and Li Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he joined Guoquan against Nanjing, urged concentrating first on Jiufuzhou to cut northern supplies, and helped drive off the relief columns of Li Xiucheng and Li Shixian.

sentences.zh: 二年，城圍合，湜當西路，克江東橋、七甕橋、紫金山諸隘，賜號著勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second year the siege ring closed; Shi held the western route, captured Jiangdong Bridge, Qiweng Bridge, and the passes of Zijin Mountain, and was granted the title Zhuoyong Babaturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 the siege closed; Shi held the west, took Jiangdong Bridge, Qiweng Bridge, and the Zijin Mountain passes, and received the title Zhuoyong Babaturu.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，克江寧，湜入旱西門，遇李秀成率死黨出走，逆擊反奔，尋為他軍所擒，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year Jiangning was taken; Shi entered the Hanxi Gate, met Li Xiucheng leading diehards in flight, struck back and drove them to flee in reverse, and soon he was captured by another army; Shi was placed on the register for provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1864 Nanjing fell; Shi entered the Hanxi Gate, met Li Xiucheng fleeing with his diehards, drove them back, and though Li was soon taken by another column, Shi was placed on the register for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，授陝西按察使，調山西。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Shaanxi provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was appointed Shaanxi provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 捻匪方熾，陳籌防五策，建水師於龍門、砥柱間。

translations.literal: Nian rebels were then at their height; he memorialized five plans for defense and established a naval force between Longmen and Dizhu.
translations.idiomatic: With the Nian at their height, he proposed five defensive measures and built a river force between Longmen and Dizhu.

sentences.zh: 五年，捻酋張總愚謀渡渭，湜令水師焚三河口浮橋，督民團備渭北，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Nian chieftain Zhang Zongyu planned to cross the Wei; Shi ordered the naval force to burn the pontoon bridge at Sanhekou, supervised militia to guard north of the Wei, and the rebels could not carry out their plan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Nian leader Zhang Zongyu tried to cross the Wei; Shi burned the pontoon at Sanhekou, rallied militia on the north bank, and blocked him.

sentences.zh: 六年，命湜駐汾州，節制文武。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to station at Fenzhou and command civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was ordered to Fenzhou to command civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 冬，總愚乘河冰合，竄入山西，七年春，犯畿輔。

translations.literal: That winter Zongyu took advantage of the frozen river to flee into Shanxi; in the spring of the seventh year he invaded the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zongyu crossed the ice into Shanxi; in the spring of 1868 he struck the capital region.

sentences.zh: 湜以疏防褫職，譴戍新疆，巡撫鄭敦謹疏請留防。

translations.literal: Shi was stripped of office for lax defense and condemned to service in Xinjiang; Governor Zheng Dunjin memorialized requesting that he be kept for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was stripped of office for lax defense and ordered to Xinjiang; Governor Zheng Dunjin asked that he be kept for defense duty.

sentences.zh: 冬，陝回將乘隙渡河，屢擊走之，詔免發遣。

translations.literal: That winter Shaanxi Muslim rebels were about to seize an opening to cross the river; he repeatedly drove them off, and an edict exempted him from banishment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Shaanxi Muslim rebels tried to cross the river; he drove them off repeatedly, and the court canceled his banishment.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠西征，檄湜率五營出固原，斷漢伯堡賊南趨河州之道，殲餘彥祿餘黨於羅家嶮。

translations.literal: When Zuo Zongtang marched west, he ordered Shi to lead five battalions out from Guyuan, cut the route by which Hanbobao rebels might move south toward Hezhou, and destroyed the remnant followers of Yu Yanlu at Luojiajian.
translations.idiomatic: On Zuo Zongtang's western campaign, Shi led five battalions from Guyuan, blocked the rebels' route south toward Hezhou, and destroyed Yu Yanlu's remnants at Luojiajian.

sentences.zh: 九年，金積堡平，復原官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jinjibao was pacified and he recovered his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 Jinjibao fell and he recovered his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十年，進規河州，宗棠令湜盡護諸將渡洮進攻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he advanced against Hezhou; Zongtang ordered Shi to escort all the generals in crossing the Tao to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he advanced on Hezhou; Zongtang had him escort the generals across the Tao.

sentences.zh: 連克陳家山、楊家山、董家山諸回堡，逼攻太子寺老巢，破其外壕。

translations.literal: He took in succession the Muslim forts of Chenjiashan, Yangjiashan, and Dongjiashan, pressed the attack on the old nest at Taizisi, and broke its outer moat.
translations.idiomatic: He took Chenjiashan, Yangjiashan, and Dongjiashan, pressed Taizisi, and breached its outer defenses.

sentences.zh: 十一年，提督傅先宗等戰歿，賊乘勝來攻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Regional Commander Fu Xianzong and others died in battle; the rebels seized the victory to come and attack.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 Regional Commander Fu Xianzong was killed; the rebels pressed their advantage.

sentences.zh: 湜陽置酒高會，密令總兵沈玉遂急搗之，馬占鼇窮蹙乞降，縛悍酋狗齒牙子等以獻。

translations.literal: Shi openly set out wine in high festivity while secretly ordering Brigadier-General Shen Yusui to strike them in haste; Ma Zhan'ao, pressed to extremity, begged to surrender; fierce chieftains Gou Chiya and others were bound and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Shi held a feast openly while secretly ordering Brigadier Shen Yusui to strike; Ma Zhan'ao, cornered, surrendered; fierce leaders including Gou Chiya were bound and sent in.

sentences.zh: 河州平。

translations.literal: Hezhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二年，叛酋馬桂源、馬本源踞巴燕戎格，湜率軍進討，二酋敗遁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year rebel chieftains Ma Guiyuan and Ma Benyuan held Bayan Rongge; Shi led his army to attack and the two chieftains were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 rebels Ma Guiyuan and Ma Benyuan held Bayan Rongge; Shi attacked and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 湜善視其孥，遂因佔鼇來降，數其罪誅之，並斬馬五麻諸悍目，賜號奇車伯巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Shi treated their families well; then through Zhan'ao they came to surrender; he enumerated their crimes and executed them, also beheading fierce officers such as Ma Wuma, and was granted the title Qichebo Babaturu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi treated their families well; Zhan'ao then came in; Shi condemned and executed the leaders, beheaded hard fighters including Ma Wuma, and received the title Qichebo Babaturu.

sentences.zh: 四月，逾河收循化。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he crossed the river and recovered Xunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he crossed the river and recovered Xunhua.

sentences.zh: 循化撒拉回素獷悍，恃險擾邊。

translations.literal: The Salar Muslims of Xunhua had always been fierce and bold, relying on difficult terrain to harass the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Salar Muslims of Xunhua were notoriously fierce and had long raided the frontier from the mountains.

sentences.zh: 湜深入其阻，群回縛悍目馬十八、沈五十七等二十餘人獻軍前，繳械受約束。

translations.literal: Shi penetrated deep into their strongholds; the Hui masses bound fierce officers Ma Shiba, Shen Wushiqi, and more than twenty others and presented them before the army; arms were surrendered and they accepted restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Shi penetrated their strongholds; the communities bound more than twenty hard fighters including Ma Shiba and Shen Wushiqi and handed them over; they surrendered arms and submitted to control.

sentences.zh: 湜規地勢，修城設官，分營扼駐，與西寧、碾伯、河州聲息相通焉。

translations.literal: Shi surveyed the terrain, repaired walls and established officials, divided camps to hold key points, and was in communication with Xining, Nianbo, and Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi surveyed the ground, rebuilt walls, posted officials, garrisoned key points, and linked communications with Xining, Nianbo, and Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋謝軍事回籍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he resigned from military affairs and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left military service and returned home.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，兩江總督曾國荃奏調統水陸諸軍，兼治海防，駐軍吳淞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu, Liangjiang Governor Zeng Guoquan memorialized to transfer him to command all land and river forces, also oversee coastal defense, and station troops at Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 Liangjiang Governor Zeng Guoquan had him command land and river forces, oversee coastal defense, and camp at Wusong.

sentences.zh: 以私行遊宴被劾歸。

translations.literal: He was impeached for private outings and banquets and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached for private outings and feasting and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復出統南洋兵輪，總湘、淮諸軍營務，授江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he came out again to command the Southern Ocean gunboats, oversee Hunan and Huai army camp affairs, and was appointed Jiangsu provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 he returned to command the southern gunboats, oversee Hunan and Huai camp affairs, and was made Jiangsu provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遼東兵事起，詔集舊部防山海關，移屯關外鞍山站。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year war broke out in Liaodong; an edict gathered his old troops to defend Shanhaiguan, and he moved to encamp outside the pass at Anshan Station.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 war broke out in Liaodong; the court recalled his old troops to Shanhaiguan, and he moved to Anshan Station beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，進駐大高嶺，遣將援遼陽。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year he advanced to station at Dagao Ridge and sent generals to aid Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1895 he advanced to Dagao Ridge and sent generals to relieve Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 和議成，擢江西布政使。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he was promoted to Jiangxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he was promoted to Jiangxi provincial administration commissioner.
