sentences.zh: 命剿甘肅叛回，未行，复駐山海關。

translations.literal: He was ordered to suppress rebellious Muslims in Gansu; before he could depart he was again stationed at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to suppress Gansu rebels but was sent back to Shanhaiguan before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1896 and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 湜從曾國荃最久，後屢蹶，仕久不進。

translations.literal: Shi followed Zeng Guoquan the longest, but afterward stumbled repeatedly and for long made no advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had served Zeng Guoquan longest, but later stumbled repeatedly and advanced slowly in office.

sentences.zh: 世稱為宿將，光緒中，命繪中興功臣於紫光閣，徵集諸將之像，湜與焉。

translations.literal: The age called him a veteran general; in the Guangxu reign, when the court ordered portraits of Restoration merit subjects painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor and collected images of the generals, Shi was among them.
translations.idiomatic: He was regarded as a veteran; in the Guangxu reign, when the court painted Restoration heroes in the Hall of Purple Splendor, his portrait was included.

sentences.zh: 李元度，字次青，湖南平江人。

translations.literal: Li Yuandu, styled Ciqing, was a man of Pingjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuandu, whose courtesy name was Ciqing, came from Pingjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以舉人官黔陽教諭。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he served as instructor at Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served as instructor at Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓在籍治團練，元度上書數千言言兵事，國籓壯之，招入幕。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan organized local militia in his native place, Yuandu submitted a memorial of several thousand characters on military affairs; Guofan was impressed and recruited him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan organized local militia at home, Yuandu sent a long memorial on military affairs; Guofan was impressed and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，國籓移軍江西，令元度募勇三千屯湖口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng Guofan moved his army to Jiangxi and ordered Yuandu to raise three thousand braves and encamp at Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 Guofan moved to Jiangxi and had Yuandu raise three thousand men at Hukou.

sentences.zh: 六年，移屯撫州，偕江軍林源恩合防。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he moved to encamp at Fuzhou and together with Jiang Army commander Lin Yuan'en joined in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he moved to Fuzhou and joined Jiang Army commander Lin Yuan'en in the defense.

sentences.zh: 與賊相持久之，餉絀，分軍克宜黃、崇仁；

translations.literal: He faced the rebels in a prolonged standoff; supplies ran short; he divided his army and captured Yihuang and Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: He faced the rebels in a long standoff; supplies ran short; he sent columns that took Yihuang and Chongren.

sentences.zh: 而賊自景德來援，撫州賊出攻江軍營，林源恩死之。

translations.literal: But rebels came from Jingde to aid them; Fuzhou rebels sallied out to attack the Jiang Army camp, and Lin Yuan'en died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came from Jingde to relieve them; Fuzhou rebels struck the Jiang Army camp and killed Lin Yuan'en.

sentences.zh: 元度突圍出，移屯貴溪，防廣信。

translations.literal: Yuandu broke out of the encirclement, moved to encamp at Guixi, and defended Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu broke out, moved to Guixi, and held Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 七年，賊二萬來襲玉山，守卒僅七百人，元度迎戰，斷賊浮梁，賊以步隊綴軍，騎賊趨上游跐水渡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year twenty thousand rebels came to assault Yushan; the garrison was only seven hundred men; Yuandu met them in battle, cut off their pontoon bridge, the rebels used infantry to delay the army while cavalry hurried upstream to wade across the water.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 twenty thousand rebels struck Yushan, defended by only seven hundred men; Yuandu fought them, destroyed their pontoon, while infantry pinned him and cavalry forded upstream.

sentences.zh: 乃回城拒守，被攻兩晝夜，元度立埤兒間，彈中左頰。

translations.literal: He then returned to the city to hold defense; they were attacked for two days and nights; Yuandu stood among the battlements and was struck by a bullet in the left cheek.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back into the city and held out under assault for two days and nights; standing on the wall he was shot in the left cheek.

sentences.zh: 賊忽罷攻，鉦鐃雜作，知其穴地道，乃掘壕以防，伺其穿隧及壕殪之。

translations.literal: The rebels suddenly ceased the attack and gongs and cymbals sounded together; knowing they were mining a tunnel, he dug a trench as defense, waited until they tunneled to the trench, and killed them there.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suddenly stopped and beat gongs and cymbals; guessing a mine, he dug a trench, waited for the tunnel to reach it, and killed the miners.

sentences.zh: 賊技窮引去，伏兵邀擊，安仁、弋陽、廣信皆平。

translations.literal: The rebels, their stratagems exhausted, withdrew; ambush troops intercepted them; Anren, Yiyang, and Guangxin were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Their tricks exhausted, the rebels withdrew; ambushes hit them on the way; Anren, Yiyang, and Guangxin were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 元度先已累擢知府，以道員記名，至是加按察使銜，賜號色爾固楞巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Yuandu had already been repeatedly promoted to prefect and placed on the register as circuit commissioner; now he was given the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and granted the title Seerguleng Babaturu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu had already risen to prefect and been placed on the register as circuit commissioner; now he received the nominal rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and the title Seerguleng Babaturu.

sentences.zh: 八年，率所部平江軍援浙江，敗賊玉山子午口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he led his Pingjiang Army to aid Zhejiang and defeated rebels at Ziwukou in Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he led his Pingjiang troops to aid Zhejiang and routed the rebels at Ziwukou in Yushan.

sentences.zh: 會克常山、江山，授浙江溫處道。

translations.literal: He joined in capturing Changshan and Jiangshan and was appointed intendant of the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Changshan and Jiangshan and was appointed intendant of the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十年，曾國籓督師皖南，調元度安徽寧池太道，防徽州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zeng Guofan commanded the army in southern Anhui; Yuandu was transferred to the Ning-Guichi-Taiping intendant post in Anhui to defend Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Zeng Guofan commanded in southern Anhui; Yuandu was transferred to defend Huizhou as Anhui intendant of the Ning-Guichi-Taiping circuit.

sentences.zh: 至甫三日，賊由旌德糾合土匪散軍入績溪叢山關。

translations.literal: He had been there only three days when rebels from Jingde gathered local bandits and scattered troops and entered Congshan Pass in Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: He had been there only three days when rebels from Jingde, bandits, and scattered troops entered Congshan Pass in Jixi.

sentences.zh: 遣同知童梅華、都司單綏福率千人往援，敗挫。

translations.literal: He sent Subprefect Tong Meihua and Commandant Dan Suifu with a thousand men to aid them, and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Subprefect Tong Meihua and Commandant Dan Suifu with a thousand men; they were beaten.

sentences.zh: 賊趨郡城，元度退走。

translations.literal: The rebels moved toward the prefectural city and Yuandu retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels moved on the prefectural seat and Yuandu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 國籓奏劾，褫職逮治。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized to impeach him; his office was stripped and he was arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan impeached him; he was stripped of office and arrested.

sentences.zh: 會浙江巡撫王有齡奏調援浙，元度不待命，回籍募勇八千，號安越軍。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang Governor Wang Youling memorialized to transfer troops to aid Zhejiang, Yuandu did not await orders, returned home to raise eight thousand braves, and called them the Anyue Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang Governor Wang Youling called for aid, Yuandu did not wait for orders, went home, raised eight thousand men, and called them the Anyue Army.

sentences.zh: 將行，粵匪犯湖南，巡撫文格留其軍守瀏陽，偕諸軍破賊，詔賞還按察使銜，並加布政使銜。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Guangdong rebels invaded Hunan; Governor Wenge kept his army to defend Liuyang; together with other armies he defeated the rebels; an edict rewarded him by restoring his provincial surveillance commissioner rank and also adding the provincial administration commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Guangdong rebels struck Hunan; Governor Wenge kept his army at Liuyang; with other forces he beat them; the court restored his surveillance commissioner's rank and added the administration commissioner's rank.

sentences.zh: 會杭州陷，王有齡死，詔左宗棠代之。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youling died, an edict appointed Zuo Zongtang in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youling died, the court appointed Zuo Zongtang in his place.

sentences.zh: 元度率軍入浙，與李定太守衢州，授浙江鹽運使，署布政使。

translations.literal: Yuandu led his army into Zhejiang, joined Li Ding in defending Quzhou, was appointed Zhejiang salt transport commissioner, and acted as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu marched into Zhejiang, joined Li Ding in holding Quzhou, was made Zhejiang salt transport commissioner, and acted as provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 國籓以元度罪未定，不聽勘遽回籍，复劾革職，交左宗棠差遣。

translations.literal: Guofan, because Yuandu's guilt was not yet settled, impeached him again for returning home without awaiting investigation, stripped him of office, and handed him over to Zuo Zongtang for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan, saying his case was still open, impeached him again for leaving without awaiting trial, stripped him of office, and placed him under Zuo Zongtang.

sentences.zh: 言官再論劾，命國籓、宗棠按治。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached him again; Guofan and Zongtang were ordered to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him again; Guofan and Zongtang were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 國籓奏：「徽州之失，元度甫至，情有可原。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized: "In the loss of Huizhou, Yuandu had only just arrived, and the circumstances admit of excuse."
translations.idiomatic: Guofan wrote, "The loss of Huizhou came only three days after Yuandu arrived, which admits of excuse."

sentences.zh: 」宗棠疏言：「杭州失陷，非因其逗留所致。

translations.literal: Zongtang memorialized: "The fall of Hangzhou was not caused by his delay."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo wrote, "Hangzhou did not fall because he delayed."

sentences.zh: 惟落職後求去索餉，不顧大局。

translations.literal: "But after losing office he sought to leave and demanded pay without regard for the larger situation."
translations.idiomatic: "But after losing office he demanded pay and tried to leave without regard to the larger situation."

sentences.zh: 」論遣戍。

translations.literal: He was sentenced to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to banishment.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨、李鴻章、彭玉麟、鮑超等交章薦其才，代繳台費，免罪歸。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen, Li Hongzhang, Peng Yulin, Bao Chao, and others submitted successive memorials commending his talent, paid his fine on his behalf, and he was pardoned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen, Li Hongzhang, Peng Yulin, Bao Chao, and others repeatedly recommended his talent, paid his fine for him, and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 同治初，貴州巡撫張亮基奏起剿教匪，以功復原官，擢雲南按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, Guizhou Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized to recall him to suppress sectarian rebels; through merit he recovered his original office and was promoted to Yunnan provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign Guizhou Governor Zhang Liangji recalled him to fight sectarian rebels; on merit he recovered his rank and was promoted to Yunnan provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu he observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補貴州按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Guizhou provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Guizhou surveillance commissioner and then administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1887.

sentences.zh: 元度擅文章，好言兵，然自將屢僨事。

translations.literal: Yuandu excelled at literary composition and loved to discourse on military affairs, yet when he himself commanded he repeatedly failed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu was a fine writer and loved to talk of war, yet in command he failed again and again.

sentences.zh: 所著先正事略、天嶽山館文集，並行世。

translations.literal: His works Xianzheng Shilue and Tianyue Shanguan Wenji both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works Xianzheng Shilue and Tianyue Shanguan Wenji both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蕭啟江、張運蘭功在江西，在湘軍中資勞最深，中道而殞，故卹典特隆。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Xiao Qijiang and Zhang Yunlan achieved merit in Jiangxi; among the Hunan Army their seniority and service were deepest; they died mid-course, and therefore mourning rites were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Xiao Qijiang and Zhang Yunlan won their fame in Jiangxi; among the Hunan Army they ranked highest in seniority and service; they died in mid-career, and so received especially generous mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 唐訓方、蔣凝學轉戰功多，舊部散亡，再出遂不競。

translations.literal: Tang Xunfang and Jiang Ningxue fought in many campaigns with great merit, but their old troops dispersed; when they came out again they could not compete.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xunfang and Jiang Ningxue fought widely and well, but their old commands had scattered, and on their return they could not regain their standing.

sentences.zh: 陳湜、李元度皆躓而復起。

translations.literal: Chen Shi and Li Yuandu both stumbled and rose again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi and Li Yuandu both fell and rose again.

sentences.zh: 元度文學之士，所行不逮其言，軍中猶以宿望推之爾。

translations.literal: Yuandu was a man of letters; his conduct did not match his words, yet in the army he was still esteemed for long-standing reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu was a literary man whose deeds did not match his words; the army still deferred to him for his long-standing name.
